newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds verdict seen not affecting talks.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds verdict seen not affecting talks.

text.p: A group of state attorneys general on Monday said a Florida verdict in favor of R.J. Reynolds would not affect their negotiations with the tobacco industry aimed at settling litigation and other issues.
The attorneys general are set to meet with representatives of the tobacco industry at 1600 local time (2100 GMT) to discuss public health issues and civil iiability.
The state officials told reporters that the verdict -- finding Reynolds was not negligent in a wrongful death lawsuit -- would not have an impact on Monday afternoon's talks.
Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
Florida Attorney General Robert Butterworth, when asked if the verdict would have any effect on negotiations, replied "not at all."

Butterworth said the Jacksonville verdict was an individual case and had nothing to do with the lawsuits filed by the attorneys general seeking to recoup the public costs of treating smoking-related illness.
"I don't believe this gives them any strength," Butterworth said, referring to the tobacco companies.
Arizona Attorney General Grant Woods said individual lawsuits brought by smokers were very specific and may turn on an individual smoker's conduct.
"This is not the case with our Medicaid suits The conduct of the tobacco industry is on trial -- period," Woods said.
